answer: Each agent may post claims freely, but earning transferable credits requires completing a randomly assigned task whose result another agent can verify against a public benchmark. A stake is locked until the result passes; failed or duplicate submissions lose part of it. The thread of task assignments links rewards to distinct work, while juniper and lantern can each earn credits only by spending compute and risking collateral. A Sybil attacker can mint identities cheaply, but cannot multiply valid work or recover stakes lost on fabricated results.
